```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(plotly)

baby_names <- read_csv("ssa-baby-names.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# Full historical yearly aggregation (1916-2025) - no observations filtered out
dustin_yearly <- baby_names |>
  filter(toupper(name) == "DUSTIN") |>
  summarize(count = sum(count), .by = year) |>
  arrange(year)

# Summary metrics computed from the complete unfiltered dataset
first_obs_year <- min(dustin_yearly$year)
last_obs_year <- max(dustin_yearly$year)
total_all_time <- sum(dustin_yearly$count)
total_since_1960 <- dustin_yearly |>
  filter(year >= 1960) |>
  pull(count) |>
  sum()
pct_since_1960 <- (total_since_1960 / total_all_time) * 100

peak_row <- dustin_yearly |> slice_max(count, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
peak_year <- peak_row$year
peak_count <- peak_row$count

count_1960 <- dustin_yearly |> filter(year == 1960) |> pull(count)
count_last <- dustin_yearly |> filter(year == last_obs_year) |> pull(count)
```

<div class="dashboard-card">
<h2>Annual U.S. Births Named Dustin (1960–2026 Axis Window)</h2>
<div class="card-subtitle">Combined female and male births recorded by the Social Security Administration. The x-axis spans <strong>1960 to 2026</strong>; observed data runs through <strong>2025</strong> (the latest published SSA release), with the unreleased 2026 period shaded.</div>

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| fig-dpi: 300
#| fig-alt: "Line chart showing annual U.S. babies named Dustin from 1960 to 2026. Births rose from 53 in 1960 to a peak of 10,520 in 1985, then declined to 365 in 2025, with 2026 shaded as not yet released."

x_breaks <- c(seq(1960, 2020, by = 5), 2026)

dustin_yearly |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = count)) +
  # Shaded region distinguishing last observed year (2025) from 2026 axis boundary
  annotate(
    "rect",
    xmin = 2025, xmax = 2026,
    ymin = 0, ymax = 11600,
    fill = "#e2e8f0", alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 2025,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "#64748b",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_area(fill = "#0072B2", alpha = 0.12) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.15, color = "#0072B2") +
  # Highlight key observations: 1985 peak and 2025 last observed year
  geom_point(
    data = dustin_yearly |> filter(year %in% c(peak_year, last_obs_year)),
    aes(x = year, y = count),
    color = c("#D55E00", "#0072B2"),
    size = c(3.4, 2.8)
  ) +
  annotate(
    "label",
    x = peak_year, y = peak_count + 550,
    label = paste0("Peak (", peak_year, "): ", comma(peak_count), " babies"),
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 3.5,
    color = "#9a3412",
    fill = "#fff7ed",
    label.size = 0.3
  ) +
  annotate(
    "label",
    x = 2024.4, y = count_last + 1150,
    label = paste0("Last observed (", last_obs_year, "): ", comma(count_last)),
    hjust = 1,
    size = 3.2,
    color = "#0f172a",
    fill = "#f8fafc",
    label.size = 0.25
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 2024.7, y = 9800,
    label = "2026 data not yet\nreleased by SSA →",
    hjust = 1,
    size = 3.1,
    color = "#475569",
    fontface = "italic"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = x_breaks,
    labels = label_number(accuracy = 1, big.mark = "")
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 10000, by = 2000),
    labels = label_comma()
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(
    xlim = c(1960, 2026),
    ylim = c(0, 11600),
    expand = FALSE
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Babies Named Dustin in the U.S. (1960–2026)",
    subtitle = "Annual births surged during the late 1960s–1980s, peaking at 10,520 in 1985 before declining through 2025",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Number of Babies",
    caption = "Source: U.S. Social Security Administration. Observations span 1916–2025; no 2026 data has been published."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15, color = "#0f172a", margin = margin(b = 4)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, color = "#475569", margin = margin(b = 14)),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "#64748b", hjust = 0, margin = margin(t = 12)),
    axis.title.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11, color = "#1e293b", margin = margin(t = 10)),
    axis.title.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11, color = "#1e293b", margin = margin(r = 10)),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10, color = "#334155"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "#f1f5f9", linewidth = 0.4),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "#e2e8f0", linewidth = 0.5),
    plot.margin = margin(10, 18, 10, 10)
  )
```

<h2>Interactive Year-by-Year Explorer (1960–2026)</h2>
<div class="card-subtitle">Hover over any point along the curve to inspect exact annual birth counts from the SSA dataset.</div>

```{r}
dustin_window <- dustin_yearly |>
  filter(year >= 1960)

plot_ly(
  data = dustin_window,
  x = ~year,
  y = ~count,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "lines+markers",
  line = list(color = "#0072B2", width = 2.5),
  marker = list(color = "#0072B2", size = 5),
  fill = "tozeroy",
  fillcolor = "rgba(0, 114, 178, 0.10)",
  hovertemplate = "<b>Year:</b> %{x:d}<br><b>Babies named Dustin:</b> %{y:,}<extra></extra>",
  name = "Observed SSA Births"
) |>
  add_markers(
    data = dustin_window |> filter(year == peak_year),
    x = ~year,
    y = ~count,
    marker = list(color = "#D55E00", size = 10, line = list(color = "#ffffff", width = 1.5)),
    hovertemplate = "<b>Peak Year (%{x:d})</b><br><b>Babies named Dustin:</b> %{y:,}<extra></extra>",
    name = "1985 Peak"
  ) |>
  layout(
    xaxis = list(
      title = "Year",
      range = c(1960, 2026),
      tickmode = "array",
      tickvals = c(seq(1960, 2020, by = 5), 2026),
      ticktext = as.character(c(seq(1960, 2020, by = 5), 2026)),
      tickformat = "d",
      gridcolor = "#f1f5f9",
      zeroline = FALSE
    ),
    yaxis = list(
      title = "Number of Babies",
      range = c(0, 11600),
      tickformat = ",",
      gridcolor = "#e2e8f0",
      zeroline = FALSE
    ),
    shapes = list(
      list(
        type = "rect",
        x0 = 2025, x1 = 2026,
        y0 = 0, y1 = 11600,
        fillcolor = "rgba(226, 232, 240, 0.65)",
        line = list(width = 0)
      ),
      list(
        type = "line",
        x0 = 2025, x1 = 2025,
        y0 = 0, y1 = 11600,
        line = list(color = "#64748b", width = 1, dash = "dash")
      )
    ),
    annotations = list(
      list(
        x = peak_year,
        y = peak_count,
        text = paste0("<b>1985 Peak: ", comma(peak_count), "</b>"),
        showarrow = TRUE,
        arrowhead = 2,
        ax = 0,
        ay = -28,
        font = list(color = "#9a3412", size = 12)
      ),
      list(
        x = 2025,
        y = count_last,
        text = paste0("Last observed (2025): ", comma(count_last)),
        showarrow = TRUE,
        arrowhead = 2,
        ax = -75,
        ay = -30,
        font = list(color = "#0f172a", size = 11)
      )
    ),
    showlegend = FALSE,
    margin = list(l = 65, r = 25, t = 20, b = 50),
    paper_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)",
    plot_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)",
    hovermode = "x unified"
  ) |>
  config(displayModeBar = FALSE, responsive = TRUE)
```

<div class="dashboard-card">
<h2>Key Findings & Data Integrity Notes</h2>
<ul class="takeaway-list">
<li><strong>Rapid climb after 1960:</strong> Only <strong>53</strong> babies were named Dustin in 1960, before the name rose steeply in the late 1960s and 1970s (reaching <strong>1,303</strong> in 1970 and <strong>8,490</strong> in 1980).</li>
<li><strong>1985 peak:</strong> Popularity reached its all-time high in <strong>1985</strong> with <strong>10,520</strong> births, remaining above 8,000 births per year through 1990 (<strong>8,488</strong>).</li>
<li><strong>Post-1990 decline to present:</strong> Annual births declined to <strong>2,629</strong> in 2000, <strong>869</strong> in 2010, <strong>404</strong> in 2020, and <strong>365</strong> in 2025.</li>
</ul>
<div class="data-note"><strong>Methodology &amp; Axis Range Note (1960–2026):</strong> All summary statistics are computed from the complete, unfiltered U.S. Social Security Administration baby names dataset, which records <strong>209,721</strong> total births named Dustin between <strong>1916 and 2025</strong> (including 578 births prior to 1960). Setting the visible x-axis window to 1960–2026 displays the modern era without excluding any historical records from summary calculations. Because the Social Security Administration has only published birth records through <strong>2025</strong>, no data is fabricated or extrapolated for 2026.</div>
</div>
